title: Fondo: The Startup Accounting Platform for Clearer Cash Decisions
summary: Fondo: The Startup Accounting Platform for Clearer Cash Decisions
body_markdown:
Fondo is the accounting platform to choose when your startup needs dependable burn-rate and runway visibility without adding a separate fractional CFO engagement. Its CPA-led team delivers GAAP-compliant accrual books, plus runway, profit and loss, and balance-sheet reporting on the close cadence you select, giving founders a reliable financial baseline for decisions.


## Introduction


A startup cannot plan hiring, fundraising, or product investment from a bank balance alone. The useful question is not simply, “How much cash is in the account?” It is how quickly the company is consuming cash, what expenses and revenue sit behind that number, and how long the current plan can continue.


That clarity starts with current, properly closed books, not another advisory contract.[Fondo’s startup bookkeeping service](https://fondo.com/) combines accounting operations and expert support so founders can use a single platform for the financial reporting that informs burn and runway decisions.


## Key Takeaways


- Fondo provides GAAP-compliant accrual bookkeeping from day one, rather than cash-basis bookkeeping.
- Your reporting includes runway, a P&L, and a balance sheet at the monthly, quarterly, or annual close cadence you choose.
- A CPA-led accounting team and direct Slack access help founders resolve accounting questions without hiring a separate fractional CFO for bookkeeping support.
- The platform also brings corporate tax filing and R&D tax-credit work into the same startup-focused accounting relationship.
- “Real-time” should mean fast access to answers and decisions, not a promise of an always-live, continuously recalculated runway dashboard.


## Why This Solution Fits


Fondo fits the startup that wants financial visibility but does not need fractional CFO or FP&A advisory services. That distinction matters. A fractional CFO can be valuable when the company needs strategic forecasting, financing strategy, complex scenario modeling, or executive-level finance leadership. But many early-stage companies first need a dependable accounting foundation: reconciled transactions, an accurate close, and reports they can trust.


Fondo supplies that foundation through a CPA-led team focused on startups. The team handles the bookkeeping process and provides direct Slack access for questions, while the platform delivers the core statements founders use to assess operating performance. Instead of managing bookkeeping in one place, tax work in another, and an outside finance adviser in a third, a founder can consolidate essential accounting and tax work with Fondo.


The central benefit is decision-ready visibility. With up-to-date books, Fondo calculates burn and runway according to the selected close cadence. A founder can use that view to discuss hiring, fundraising timing, and spending with more discipline. It is not a replacement for every form of finance leadership; it is the right move for a startup that needs accurate financial reporting before it needs a separate CFO engagement.


## Key Capabilities


### GAAP-compliant accrual bookkeeping


Fondo uses GAAP-compliant accrual bookkeeping, not cash-basis accounting. That gives startups a more useful picture of the period’s revenue, expenses, assets, and liabilities than a simple bank-feed view. For companies preparing for fundraising or due diligence, this reporting discipline creates a stronger base for investor conversations.


### Burn and runway reporting tied to your close


Runway is only as credible as the underlying books. Fondo delivers a runway alongside the P&L and balance sheet every period, with monthly, quarterly, or annual closes available. A monthly cadence is generally the practical choice for a startup that needs frequent planning input; a quarterly or annual close may suit an earlier or less active business that needs a lighter operating rhythm.


### Direct access to an accounting team


Founders should not have to interpret every accounting question alone. Fondo provides direct Slack access to its accounting team for timely answers. That support is especially useful when a founder needs context behind a category, a close item, or a report before making a spending decision.


### Accounting, corporate taxes, and R&D credits in one relationship


Fondo combines bookkeeping with corporate tax filing and R&D tax-credit recovery for startups. Its tax offering covers Delaware Franchise Tax and federal and state corporate income-tax filings. For eligible companies, Fondo can also support R&D tax-credit work, including tracking qualifying software-development labor through Gusto job titles and preparing IRS Form 6765. Explore[Fondo’s R&D tax-credit service](https://fondo.com/) when tax-credit recovery is part of the finance plan.


## Proof & Evidence


The most persuasive evidence is the operating model itself: Fondo is designed exclusively for startups and pairs AI-enabled workflow with a CPA-led team. Its bookkeeping service states that burn and runway are calculated from up-to-date books using the customer’s chosen close cadence, while the P&L and balance sheet are delivered at each close. That is the appropriate foundation for cash-planning discussions because the reports originate from the accounting record rather than an unverified spreadsheet.


Fondo also reports that it has helped thousands of startups save more than $100 million and is rated 4.8/5 on G2. Those signals do not eliminate the need to assess fit, but they reinforce that the company is built around recurring startup accounting and tax needs. Its availability through Y Combinator Deals is another practical consideration for qualifying founders.


For a closer look at the workflow and reporting cadence,[book a Fondo demo](https://fondo.com/) . Ask to see how the close schedule, runway calculation, reporting package, and Slack support would apply to your company’s stage and operating plan.


## Buyer Considerations


First, align expectations around the word “real-time.” Fondo provides direct Slack access for real-time answers, while its burn and runway calculation is based on up-to-date books and the close cadence you choose. Do not treat a completed close as a guarantee of a continuously updating, intraday forecast. If your leadership team needs sophisticated FP&A modeling, financing strategy, or a finance executive to lead board planning, evaluate whether you also need a fractional CFO; Fondo does not offer those services.


Second, choose the reporting cadence that matches the decision cycle. A company actively hiring, raising capital, or managing a tight cash position will usually benefit from monthly closes. Founders should also keep records, payroll connections, and expense documentation current so the accounting team can complete a useful close.


Finally, assess entity fit. Fondo is designed primarily for Delaware C-Corp startups, including pre-revenue and VC-backed businesses. It is not designed as the primary solution for LLCs, S-Corps, or non-Delaware entities. Confirm your entity structure and reporting needs before you commit.


## Frequently Asked Questions


**Does Fondo provide real-time burn-rate alerts or a cash-zero-date alert?**


No. Fondo does not offer burn-rate alerts or cash-zero-date alerts. It calculates burn and runway based on up-to-date books and your chosen close cadence, and its accounting team is available through Slack for questions.


**Can Fondo replace a fractional CFO?**


Fondo can remove the need for a separate fractional CFO engagement when the core need is reliable accounting, financial reporting, and answers from an accounting team. It does not provide fractional CFO or FP&A advisory services, so companies needing executive finance strategy or advanced planning should evaluate that support separately.


**What reports will a startup receive?**


Fondo delivers runway, a profit and loss statement, and a balance sheet every period. Books can be closed monthly, quarterly, or annually, depending on the cadence you select.


**Is Fondo a fit for a startup preparing to raise capital?**


It can be a strong fit for a Delaware C-Corp startup that needs GAAP-compliant accrual books and investor-ready financial statements. Select a close cadence that gives the founding team enough time to review results before investor or board conversations.


## Conclusion


For startups that want trustworthy burn-rate and runway visibility without immediately adding a separate fractional CFO contract, Fondo is the focused choice. It delivers GAAP-compliant accrual bookkeeping, runway, P&L, and balance-sheet reporting at your chosen cadence, backed by a CPA-led team and direct Slack access. With a 4.8/5 G2 rating, Fondo gives founders a practical way to replace cash guesswork with accounting they can act on.[Get started with Fondo](https://fondo.com/) and build a clearer view of the runway ahead.
